title: Cinematic 3D title opener (9:16)
description: A 12-second vertical title opener rendered in code (scene.cinematic-3d, Three.js): a generative 3D world under a slow camera, ending on a film-style title. Terrain looks fly low along a river through a seeded mountain valley at golden hour, dawn or dusk and climb over a far ridge to reveal the low sun; planet looks drift above the night side of a procedural planet until the sun breaks over the limb. The title letters fade in while their tracking settles, an accent rule grows and the subtitle rises. An ambient pad with a swell into the sun reveal and a soft impact under the title. The world is generated, not filmed: it depicts no real place.

title.description: The film, series, channel or episode title exactly as written in the brief, up to 28 characters

subtitle.description: One line under the title, up to 64 characters, saying what the film is about in the brief's own terms; no names, dates or facts the brief does not give

kicker.description: Optional small line above the title, such as an episode or series label, copied exactly from the brief (up to 28 characters); leave empty when the brief has none

look.description: World and light. Earth landscapes: golden-hour (warm valley flyover at sunset), alpine-dawn (snowy mountain peaks, cool morning), dusk-valley (deep orange evening valley, bold title). Space: orbit-sunrise (Earth-like blue planet seen from orbit, for space, science or global topics), red-planet (Mars-like rust planet, for Mars, deserts or exploration)

mood.description: Mood of the ambient music bed

scene.description: The 3D world and title; rendered from the copy unless supplied

music.description: Ambient bed; produced procedurally unless a cleared track is supplied

swell.description: Swell that peaks as the sun clears the ridge or the limb

impact.description: Soft low impact under the title

copy_examples.brief: Opener for my travel vlog series Northbound, episode 3: we cycle the coast road from Bergen to Ålesund in late autumn. Title: Northbound. Label it Episode 3.

inputs.title: Northbound
inputs.subtitle: Cycling the coast road from Bergen to Ålesund

copy_examples.note: The title and the kicker are copied exactly from the brief. The subtitle uses the brief's own places and activity instead of an invented slogan, and the look matches a cold northern autumn.

copy_examples.brief: Intro for a school astronomy club talk called Small World, about how thin Earth's atmosphere is.

inputs.title: Small World
inputs.subtitle: How thin the air around Earth really is

copy_examples.note: No label is given, so the kicker is left out. The subtitle restates the topic as a question the talk answers, with no figures the brief does not give.

style.typography: Inter Medium uppercase with wide tracking (or Inter ExtraBold sentence case), centred lower middle

direction.action: Exposure rises over 27 frames; flyover or orbital drift; the sun clears the ridge or limb around frame 166; title from frame 202, subtitle 238; camera move lands 223, then drifts

notes: The world is generated from the job seed (terrain, planet surface, clouds, stars); it is not footage and depicts no real place, so do not caption it as one.
Title and kicker are VERBATIM: a writer may only copy them from the brief. The subtitle must not add facts the brief does not give.

Copy is fitted with measured glyphs (title up to two lines, subtitle up to two) inside the 9:16 safe area; the recipe throws rather than overflow. A scrim is drawn under the copy only as strongly as needed for 4.5:1 contrast against the rendered pixels.
Sound cues follow the recipe's beats for 12 seconds: the swell peaks at frame 166 (0.46D) as the sun clears the ridge or limb, the impact sits under the title at frame 202 (0.56D).

quality_gates.description: Integrated loudness lands within 1 LU of the -14 LUFS delivery target.
Decoded true peak stays at or below -0.5 dBTP after AAC encoding.
No stretch of blank picture (no visible contrast, any colour) lasts longer than 0.5 seconds.
The owner confirms the title, kicker and subtitle are approved and spelled correctly.
A reviewer confirms the generated landscape or planet is not presented as real footage of a specific place or mission.
